title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
statement:
Balloons are taped to a wall that we view as the x-y plane. Each `points[i] = [xstart, xend]` gives the horizontal extent of one balloon; its height is unknown and does not matter. An arrow can be fired straight up from any point `x` on the x-axis; it flies forever and bursts every balloon with `xstart <= x <= xend` (touching an edge counts). You may fire as many arrows as you like.

Return the smallest number of arrows that bursts every balloon.
notes:
## Intuition

Some arrow has to burst the balloon that ends first. Moving that arrow right to this balloon's end never loses a hit: any balloon the arrow hit starts at or before it, and no balloon ends before the first one does, so it also covers that end. So sort by right end, fire at the first end, skip every balloon that arrow already pierces, and repeat. Trying every set of arrow positions also works, but only for tiny inputs.

## Approach

1. Sort `points` by right end `xend`.
2. Fire the first arrow at `arrowX`, the right end of the first balloon, so `arrows = 1`.
3. Walk the remaining balloons in order. If a balloon's `start` is at most `arrowX`, the current arrow already bursts it (its `end` is at least `arrowX` because of the sort).
4. Otherwise it lies entirely to the right, so fire a new arrow at its `end`, add one to `arrows` and update `arrowX`.
5. Return `arrows`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted by end: `[1,6], [2,8], [7,12], [10,16]`. The first arrow goes at `arrowX = 6`. `[2,8]` starts at 2 ≤ 6, so it is already burst. `[7,12]` starts at 7 > 6, so a second arrow goes at `12`. `[10,16]` starts at 10 ≤ 12 and is burst. The answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) extra beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- Sort by the right end, not the left end; sorting by start needs an extra `min` step to stay correct (try `[[1,10],[2,3],[4,5]]`).
- Touching counts: use `start > arrowX` for a new arrow, so `[1,2]` and `[2,3]` share one.
- In Java or C, `a[1] - b[1]` overflows for coordinates near ±2^31; compare with `Integer.compare` or explicit `<` checks.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `arrows` | arrows fired so far |
| `arrowX` | position of the most recent arrow |
| `start`, `end` | the current balloon's left and right ends |
| `i` | index of the balloon being checked |

narration.2: Order balloons by where they end, so the earliest-ending one is handled first.
narration.3: At least one arrow is needed, aimed at the first balloon.
narration.4: Fire it at that balloon's right end, as far right as possible while still hitting it.
narration.6: Check every other balloon in order of right end.
narration.7: Read the balloon's left and right ends.
narration.8: If it starts after the last arrow, that arrow misses it.
narration.10: Aim the new arrow at this balloon's right end.
narration.13: Every balloon is burst; return how many arrows that took.
